task.title: Assign metadata using a subject scheme
task.shortdesc: This procedure describes a best practice for modeling and assigning iiRDS taxonomy metadata in DITA using a project-specific subject scheme map that builds on a base map with default iiRDS classes and instances.

ul.li: You have an iiRDS base subject scheme map that contains the standard iiRDS classes and instances. The copy that ships with this plugin is stored in <DITA-OT>/plugins/org.iirds.dita.package/subjectscheme/iirds-generated-subjectscheme.ditamap.
Your root DITA map is available for editing.

context.p: A project wants to assign taxonomy-based iiRDS metadata to DITA content, for example, a product structure with components, instead of relying on plain DITA attribute values.

step.cmd: Create an empty subject scheme map that will hold your custom subclasses and instances.
In the subject scheme map, add a reference to the iiRDS base subject scheme map using a <schemeref> element.
step.info: By using a schema reference, you can easily extend existing classes in the base subject scheme.

Example:<subjectScheme> <schemeref href="iirds-generated-subjectscheme.ditamap"/> </subjectScheme> Modular subject schemes let you keep the standard iiRDS taxonomies separate from project-specific values. Create this project-specific map even if you do not yet need any project-specific classes or instances. Referencing the project-specific map instead of the generic one from the root map means you can extend the taxonomy later without changing that reference.

step.cmd: Reference the project-specific subject scheme map from the root map using a <mapref> element with processing-role="resource-only".
step.info: Example:<mapref href="product-subjectscheme.ditamap" processing-role="resource-only" toc="no"/> The plugin only resolves subject schemes that are directly referenced from the root map, independent of the value of @processing-role. Subject schemes provided to DITA-OT via the --args.resources parameter are not processed.

step.cmd: Start adding your own classes or instances in the project-specific subject scheme map. For each taxonomy, reopen the relevant iiRDS class by repeating its <topicmeta> and <resourceid> exactly as declared in the base subject scheme, and nest your own <subjectdef> elements underneath it, using a custom IRI.
step.info: Example:<subjectScheme> <schemeref href="iirds-generated-subjectscheme.ditamap"/> <subjectdef keys="iirds.Component"> <topicmeta> <navtitle>component</navtitle> <resourceid appid="http://iirds.tekom.de/iirds#Component" appname="class-iri"/> </topicmeta> <subjectdef keys="myproduct.Rotor"> <topicmeta> <navtitle>Rotor</navtitle> <resourceid appid="https://my-company.com/Component#Rotor" appname="instance-iri"/> </topicmeta> </subjectdef> </subjectdef> </subjectScheme>Nesting the custom classes and instances underneath an existing iiRDS class is very important and required for the plugin to resolve the new entries with the correct iiRDS relation. In this example, iirds.Component is a copy from the base subject scheme, while myproduct.Rotor is a custom instance.

step.cmd: Assign the new metadata values to your content: Add a <data> element with a @keyref attribute for every metadata value that you want to assign.

info.p: The @keyref value must match the @keys value of a <subjectdef>.
Place the <data> element in one of the following locations:

ul.li: In the <topicmeta> of the root map, to assign metadata to the resulting document.
In the <topicmeta> of a <topicref>, to assign metadata to the referenced topic.
In the <prolog>/<metadata> element of a topic.

step.cmd: Run the dita command to transform your DITA map using the iirds transtype.
step.info: The subjectscheme metadata handler is applied automatically together with the other default metadata handlers, unless the --iirds.metadatahandler parameter is used to restrict the set of handlers. See .

taskbody.result: The generated iiRDS package contains the metadata resolved from the subject scheme.
